title: Spell Formula 1: f-strings
lessonSummary: Wonderful! f-strings are the common tongue for all elements – shorter and clearer than + and str().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: three ways to use f-strings.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Aria"
level = 5
print(f"Hello {name}!")
print(f"You are Level {level}!")

gold = 100
bonus = 25
print(f"Your gold: {gold + bonus}")

hero = "Thorin"
character_class = "Warrior"
weapon = "Axe"
print(f"{hero} the {character_class} swings their {weapon}!")

validation.expected: Thorin the Warrior swings their Axe!

tasks.instruction: Create the variables hero = "Thorin" and gold = 100. Use an f-string to print exactly this sentence: Thorin has 100 gold.
Create gold = 100 and bonus = 25. Put the calculation directly inside the curly braces of an f-string and print exactly: Your gold: 125

title: Element 1: 🔥 Fire (str)
lessonSummary: The Fire element is yours! Text lives between quotation marks – and len() counts its letters.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: Fire elements and their type.
tasks.codeTemplate:
spell = "Fireball"
description = "A powerful fire spell"
print(f"Spell: {spell}")
print(f"Element: {type(spell)}")
print(f"The spell name has {len(spell)} letters.")

tasks.instruction: Store the spell name "Frostbolt" in a variable spell and use an f-string with len() to print exactly: Frostbolt has 9 letters.
Create a variable motto = "Courage" and use type() to print its element.

title: Element 2: 🪨 Earth (int)
lessonSummary: The Earth element is solid: whole numbers you can count and calculate with.

title: Element 3: 💧 Water (float)
lessonSummary: The Water element flows: decimal numbers for damage, percentages and everything in between.

print(f"Element: {type(damage)}")
print(f"Double damage: {damage * 2}")

lessonSummary: The Air element is either there or not: True or False – the basis for every decision.

title: Fusing Elements
lessonSummary: Fusion done! Numbers calculate, texts join – and each element has its own rules.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: fusing numbers and texts.
tasks.codeTemplate:
gold_a = 150
gold_b = 75
print(f"Total gold: {gold_a + gold_b}")
print(f"Difference: {gold_a - gold_b}")
print(f"Double gold: {gold_a * 2}")

first_name = "Luna"
last_name = "Silvermoon"
full_name = first_name + " " + last_name
print(f"Full name: {full_name}")
print(f"Name x3: {first_name * 3}")

Create name = "Luna" and print the name three times in a row (using *), so the output contains: LunaLunaLuna

title: Conversion Spells: int(), float(), str(), bool()
lessonSummary: You can now transform elements: int(), float(), str() and bool() change one nature into another.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: converting elements.
tasks.codeTemplate:
age_str = "25"
age_int = int(age_str)
print(f"Age as Fire element: {age_str} ({type(age_str)})")
print(f"Age as Earth element: {age_int} ({type(age_int)})")
print(f"Age as Water element: {float(age_int)}")
print("Level: " + str(7))
print(bool(0), bool("Aria"))

tasks.instruction: Convert the text "40" into a number with int(), add 2 and print exactly: Result: 42
Convert the text "7.5" into a decimal number with float(), add 1 and print exactly: Result: 8.5
Create level = 7 and use + and str() (not an f-string!) to print exactly: Level: 7

title: Consulting the Oracle: input()
lessonSummary: The oracle has spoken! input() always gives Fire – convert the answer with int() or float() when you need a number.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and answer the oracle's questions (enter a name and a level as a number).
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = input("What is your hero's name? ")
level = int(input("What level are they? "))

print(f"Welcome, {name}!")
print(f"In 5 levels you will reach level {level + 5}.")
